NEW DELHI: The Election Commission on Thursday announced a Special Summary Revision (SSR) of electoral rolls in six states and Union territories, including Arunachal Pradesh, Chandigarh, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu, Mizoram, Odisha and Sikkim.The exercise aims to ensure that all eligible citizens are enrolled in the electoral rolls, with a particular focus on young and first-time voters. It will also facilitate advance applications from individuals who will turn 18 and become eligible to vote on April 1, July 1 and October 1, 2027.According to the schedule announced by the Commission, the draft electoral rolls will be published on November 30, while the final rolls are scheduled to be released on January 21, 2027.The Commission has directed the chief secretaries of the respective states and Union territories to ensure that adequate manpower and resources are made available to complete the exercise.The latest announcement comes months after the poll body unveiled Phase 3 of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in May. The third phase covered 16 states and three Union territories, including Delhi, Chandigarh and Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu.The SIR exercise was aimed at verifying the eligibility of around 36.7 crore electors and was scheduled to be conducted in phases, with the Commission taking into account the Census 2027 schedule and the availability of common field-level staff involved in both exercises.
Article Summary: The Election Commission announced a Special Summary Revision (SSR) of electoral rolls in six states and Union territories. The exercise aims to ensure that all eligible citizens are enrolled in the electoral rolls, with a particular focus on young and first-time voters. The draft electoral rolls will be published on November 30, while the final rolls are scheduled to be released on January 21, 2027.

NEW DELHI: Ravi Uppal, a prime accused in the multi-crore Mahadev online betting case, has been arrested in Dubai. The development comes days after co-accused Sourabh Chandrakar was extradited to India from Oman. Enforcement authorities have formally moved for Uppal's extradition, and sources said he is likely to be handed over soon to stand trial in India.Uppal was detained on the basis of an extradition request from India, with the CBI and ED establishing his last known location in the UAE.Uppal had briefly left the UAE for Vanuatu and acquired citizenship of the Pacific nation but failed to get his name removed from Interpol's Red Notice as the ED had opposed his plea before the Interpol Commission for Control of Files.He was arrested by Dubai police in Dec 2023 and was under house arrest but was released in Nov 2025 despite an extradition request pending since 2023. India has an extradition treaty with the UAE, and the Gulf nation had extradited high-profile accused in the past, including British national Christian Michel, wanted in the AgustaWestland VVIP chopper scam.India had sent a formal extradition request after Dubai police informed New Delhi of his arrest.However, the UAE authorities later said no extradition request had been received and released the accused. Indian agencies again located him in Dubai in May this year, and efforts were under way to bring him back.Uppal and other co-accused, including Chandrakar, had launched the Mahadev app in 2019 and managed to expand the user base significantly during the Covid pandemic. Uppal played a key role in orchestrating the gambling network by franchising thousands of branches across India and abroad on a profit-sharing basis.

Article Title: 24-hour arrest clock starts from detention, not formal arrest: Supreme Court
Article Text:

The Supreme Court has ruled that the 24-hour period within which an accused person must be produced before a judicial magistrate begins from the time of detention, and not merely from the time of formal arrest.The court held that arrest and detention are effectively the same for the purpose of this constitutional safeguard, as a person's liberty is curtailed in both situations.It observed that “any attempt to draw an artificial distinction between detention and arrest is constitutionally unsustainable”.The Supreme Court also criticised several high courts for making an artificial distinction between arrest and detention. It clarified that the requirement to produce an accused person before the nearest magistrate within 24 hours applies from the point at which the person is first detained.In another significant observation, the court ruled that the fundamental rights of an accused person must take precedence over provisions of special laws in cases involving delays in trial and the grant of bail. Referring to contradictory verdicts on bail in cases under laws such as the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA), the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act and the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), the court said the constitutional rights of an accused must be given priority.The court further observed that special laws cannot serve as a guide to interpreting the Constitution. Rather, such laws must be interpreted in accordance with constitutional principles.
Article Summary: Supreme Court rules that 24-hour period within which an accused person must be produced before a judicial magistrate begins from the time of detention. The court held that arrest and detention are effectively the same for the purpose of this constitutional safeguard, as a person's liberty is curtailed in both situations. It also criticised several high courts for making an artificial distinction between arrest and Detention.

NEW DELHI: Congress MP Rahul Gandhi fondly remembered late Punjabi singer Sidhu Moosewala at the party's 'Insaaf Rally' on Wednesday. The leader of the opposition in Lok Sabha recalled his first meeting with the singer and described him as an impressive, dynamic and talented young man. Inviting Moosewala's father onto the stage, Rahul Gandhi recounted how the singer had walked into his office with tattoos and made an impression on him even before he had heard any of his songs. He also recalled feeling that Moosewala was entering a dangerous field when he decided to join politics.Rahul said he had not known much about Moosewala when they first met a few years ago. He had not heard his music or even his voice. However, the singer's personality and the impression he made during their interaction led Rahul to induct him into the Congress."A few years ago, I met his son at my office. At that time, I did not know Sidhu Moosewala. I was meeting him for the first time and did not know much about him. He was an impressive young man. He walked into the room with tattoos. I had not heard his songs or even his voice at that time. I was only told that he was a good person, a musician, and wanted to join the Congress party . As politicians, we observe people carefully when they come to meet us.We do not rely too much on their words; we go by our feelings and what our heart tells us about them. He was a dynamic and talented young man, so I inducted him into the party."Recalling the concern he felt during that meeting, the leader of opposition said he had sensed that Moosewala was stepping into a dangerous environment by entering politics. He said he wanted to offer the young singer political protection and help him feel comfortable in the party."During our meeting, a thought suddenly crossed my mind, though nobody had told me anything about it. I felt that he was entering a dangerous field. I don't know why I got that feeling. He was a singer, a dynamic young man, and someone who did not understand politics very well. I felt I should protect him in my own way. I did not mean physical protection; that thought had not even crossed my mind. I meant political protection. He was a young man entering politics, and I wanted him to feel comfortable in that environment."Moosewala was shot dead in May 2022 in Punjab's Mansa district. His killing had triggered widespread outrage and questions over the state's law-and-order situation.Rahul Gandhi had also invoked Moosewala's memory during the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. When asked how many seats the INDIA bloc would win, he responded with a seemingly cryptic "295". The number was widely seen as a reference to Moosewala's popular song 295, adding another instance of the Congress leader's association with the late singer.Rahul Gandhi also targeted Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann and the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) government over the drug problem in the state. Questioning the party's promise to eradicate drug abuse, he asked what parts of Punjab had been freed from the menace since the AAP came to power."The Aam Aadmi Party came to power, and you placed your trust in it. Punjab trusted Bhagwant Mann and the Aam Aadmi Party. What was their promise? That they would eradicate drug abuse. I want to ask you... Where have they eradicated drugs? From which part of Punjab have they managed to eliminate the drug menace? They cannot eradicate drugs."He also alleged that Mann's breath would smell of alcohol during their interactions in Parliament. Rahul said the chief minister would sit with MPs and crack jokes early in the morning, but that the smell of alcohol would be noticeable by 11am.Clarifying that he was not questioning Mann's personal choice to consume alcohol, Rahul said a chief minister leading a campaign against drug abuse could not himself be under the influence of intoxicants."Let me tell you another story about your chief minister. When I was in the Lok Sabha, he would sit with us early in the morning and crack jokes. However, by 11 am, his breath would smell of alcohol. I am not saying that Bhagwant Mann should not consume alcohol. That is his personal matter. If he wants to drink, it is his personal choice. But if you want to fight drug abuse, your chief minister cannot be under the influence of intoxicants every evening. "
Article Summary: Rahul Gandhi fondly remembered late Punjabi singer Sidhu Moosewala at the party's 'Insaaf Rally' The leader of the opposition in Lok Sabha recalled his first meeting with the singer and described him as an impressive, dynamic and talented young man. He said he wanted to offer the young singer political protection and help him feel comfortable in the party.

NEW DELHI: The Cabinet is learnt to have approved another extension for the Commission of Inquiry into the Manipur violence , giving it another year, until May 20, 2027, to submit its report. This is the sixth extension granted to it since the commission was constituted in Sept 2023.As per the original notification issued in Sept 2023, the commission was required to submit its report by Nov 2023. Its mandate included inquiring into the causes and spread of violence and riots targeting members of different communities in Manipur on May 3, 2023, and thereafter.The commission was also tasked with examining whether there were any lapses or dereliction of duty by the authorities concerned or individuals, and whether the administrative measures taken to prevent and deal with the violence were adequate. It was also asked to examine the sequence of events leading to the violence and other related matters.The ethnic violence that erupted in Manipur on May 3, 2023, has since claimed more than 300 lives and displaced thousands of people, besides deepening divisions between the state’s Meitei and Kuki-Zo communities.The latest extension means the commission will now get nearly four years to complete an inquiry that was originally expected to conclude within months.
Article Summary: The Commission of Inquiry into the Manipur violence has been given another year to submit its report. This is the sixth extension granted to it since the commission was constituted in Sept 2023. The ethnic violence that erupted in Manipur on May 3, 2023, has since claimed more than 300 lives and displaced thousands of people.

NEW DELHI: Ravi Uppal, one of the promoters of the Mahadev online betting app, has been arrested in the United Arab Emirates, with Indian agencies now working to bring him back to face investigation, officials said on Wednesday.The arrest comes just days after another key figure in the alleged betting network, Saurabh Chandrakar, was brought to India from Oman. A Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) team returned with Chandrakar on 1 November after a court in Oman approved his extradition in a money laundering case being investigated by the Enforcement Directorate (ED).Uppal, 46, was taken into custody by authorities in Dubai on the basis of an Interpol Red Notice issued at the request of Indian investigating agencies, officials told PTI. The CBI and the ED are now coordinating efforts to secure his extradition to India.This is not the first time Uppal has come under the radar of authorities in the UAE. He was detained there in 2023, but Indian agencies later learnt that he was in Australia.Investigators have also alleged that Uppal, like Chandrakar, secured a passport from Vanuatu, an island country in the South Pacific.In its charge sheet filed in October 2023, the ED alleged that Uppal had "generated and enjoyed proceeds of crime and is involved in their concealment and layering".The agency further accused him of "looking after the delivery of the liaisoning money to the bureaucrats and politicians of Chhattisgarh through Chandrabhushan Verma, an assistant sub-inspector of police, and some others".Uppal and Chandrakar are both from Bhilai in Chhattisgarh's Durg district.Meanwhile, a special court in Raipur on Wednesday granted the CBI eight days of custody of Chandrakar for further questioning.According to the CBI, the Mahadev app, also known as Mahadev Online Book (MOB), started operating in 2019-20. Its user base reportedly grew "sharply" during the Covid-19 pandemic in 2020 and continued to increase afterwards.The app allegedly operated through thousands of panels and generated proceeds of crime estimated at Rs 80,000 crore since 2019, the agency said.

Article Title: SC: Can't become third chamber of Parliament
Article Text:

'Can't interfere in norms for SC/ST seats in house'

NEW DELHI: Refusing to blur the constitutional 'Lakshman Rekha' that separates the three organs of governance, Supreme Court Wednesday said it cannot usurp legislature's exclusive powers to interfere in the criteria for reserving an assembly or parliamentary constituency for Scheduled Castes or Scheduled Tribes."We cannot become the third chamber of Parliament," a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said while refusing to entertain a petition seeking quashing of a notification reserving Kadipur assembly constituency in UP for SCs.The CJI-led bench said identification of constituencies to reserve them for SCs or STs was the sole prerogative of the legislature and the court could not interfere in it, and suggested the petitioner could resort to protests to make elected representatives take corrective measures.The bench, which has been dealing with a large number of petitions on CJP protests, said in a lighter vein, "It is a good season for protest, dharna and 'naare baji'. You can also raise your voice (in protest) and tell the elected representatives that time is ripe for revising the criteria of reserving constituencies for the SC community and adopt the principle of rotational reservation. By approaching the constitutional court, you have dialled a wrong number.Appearing for a petitioner, senior advocate Gagan Gupta questioned the manner in which constituencies were geographically identified and reserved for SCs and asked whether "Section 9(1)(c) of the Delimitation Act, 2002, can constitutionally operate in a manner which permits the same territorial constituencies to remain reserved for SCs over successive electoral cycles without any mechanism for periodic rotation".The bench said, "Delimitation is a legislative exercise and the guidelines for carrying out that exercise cannot be tweaked by the courts. Can the judiciary mandate the Delimitation Commission to adopt rotational reservation policy while demarcating constituencies for SCs?"The SC agreed with Allahabad HC, which had said that since Articles 330 and 332 provide for reserving constituencies for SCs and STs, no general candidate could claim that his right to contest from constituencies reserved for SCs and STs was violated.
Article Summary: The CJI-led bench said identification of constituencies to reserve them for SCs or STs was the sole prerogative of the legislature and the court could not interfere in it. The bench suggested the petitioner could resort to protests to make elected representatives take corrective measures.

Article Title: SC rejects woman's plea to terminate six-month pregnancy over marital discord
Article Text:
The woman's husband opposed the termination, arguing that he too had a right over the unborn child.

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Wednesday refused to allow a woman's plea for medical termination of her pregnancy which was over six months along citing marital discord with her husband.The case came before a bench of Justices B V Nagarathna and R Mahadevan, which had expressed concern over the request during an earlier hearing on Monday.The woman's husband opposed the termination, arguing that he too had a right over the unborn child and was willing to take care of the baby after birth.The bench said the case was different from those involving rape, sexual assault or foetal abnormalities, where termination may be permitted under the law.It questioned whether marital discord or alleged mistreatment by a husband and in-laws could, by itself, be grounds for ending an advanced pregnancy.“It is normal that wife talks against husband and husband talks against wife but it does not mean that you have to terminate the pregnancy on that ground. It is not a case of sexual assault or single woman becoming pregnant. Where are we heading as a society if the wife says that she wants termination of pregnancy because of her fight with the husband and in-laws...What about the right of the father,” the bench had said on Monday.The woman, who appeared before the bench virtually, said she did not want to continue the pregnancy and wanted a divorce. Her husband, however, urged the court not to allow the termination. He told the bench that he would take custody of the child after birth and look after it.
Article Summary: The case came before a bench of Justices B V Nagarathna and R Mahadevan. The woman's husband opposed the termination, arguing that he too had a right over the unborn child. The bench said the case was different from those involving rape, sexual assault or foetal abnormalities.

Article Title: Presidential election today? Trump confuses India with Brazil, claims 125 million voted
Article Text:
Trump says "125 million Indians voted in presidential election today."

US President Donald Trump on Monday confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian “presidential election”, while also questioning the integrity of the American voting system.In a post on Truth Social, Trump wrote, “125 Million People voted today in the first round of India’s Presidential Election. The results came out shortly after the vote closed, on the same day!”He then compared the alleged election results with the US electoral process, writing, “In Detroit, Philadelphia, California, and numerous other US Cities and States, the results, with much smaller numbers, will often take weeks to Rig, I mean, calculate. Voting in America is corrupt!!!”However, India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college and not through a direct nationwide popular vote.Trump's remarks came after Brazil held the first round of its presidential election on Sunday, with incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and right-wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaro advancing to the October 25 runoff.With 99.99% of the votes counted, Bolsonaro secured 47.03% of the valid votes, while Lula received 45.16%, according to Brazil's Superior Electoral Court.The figure of around 125 million mentioned by Trump is close to Brazil's total valid votes, which stood at about 125.27 million, suggesting he may have confused the Brazilian election with India.Neither Bolsonaro nor Lula crossed the 50% threshold required to win in the first round, triggering the October 25 runoff, BBC reported.Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of former Brazilian president Jair Bolsonaro, outperformed expectations in the first round and finished ahead of Lula. His strong showing has raised the prospect of a shift to the right in Latin America's largest economy.Brazil has used electronic voting for decades, and electoral authorities said the first-round voting process proceeded smoothly.The Organization of American States' electoral observation mission said “the voting has been going smoothly and under adequate safety conditions.”The rapid announcement of results has also been cited as a strength of Brazil's electronic voting system.“When results take a lot of time, it creates an opening for people to cast doubt on the results, to say there’s been a problem,” Josemar Lauriano Pereira, a 46-year-old lawyer in Rio de Janeiro, told the Associated Press.Trump's post drew reactions on social media, with users pointing out that India does not elect its president through a direct popular vote.One user posted, “Trump living in a different world? Is a presidential election taking place in India? President Donald Trump made the incorrect claim that 125 million people voted in India's "presidential election" today.”Another said, “What is my blud Donald Trump smoking? Why is he mentioning India instead of Brazil when talking about the election?”
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian "presidential election" He also questioned the integrity of the American voting system. India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college.

NEW DELHI: Virat Kohli made batting look easy in India's first ODI against New Zealand in Auckland on Wednesday. The star batter scored 74 runs off 51 balls to help India win the match by five wickets (DLS) and take a 1-0 lead in the five-match series.India had to chase a revised target of 143 runs in 32 overs. Kohli made sure there was no late drama as India reached the target in just 22.4 overs.Kohli hit 13 fours and a six during his innings. His shots through the covers and pulls were among the highlights of his knock.Former India head coach Ravi Shastri was full of praise for Kohli. He said the 74-run innings was as valuable as a century because of the conditions in which it was played."A 70 in conditions like these is worth a hundred. He never got ahead of himself throughout the innings. And when he stays in fourth gear like this, then God help you. When the youngsters in the dressing room watch him and how he still gets angry at getting out at 38, they'll understand they have work to do," Ravi Shastri said on Sony Sports.Shastri also spoke about the support Kohli gave captain Shubman Gill during the chase.According to him, Kohli's ability to take quick singles kept the New Zealand bowlers under pressure."He also took a lot of pressure off Shubman Gill at the other end. He gets off strike so quickly that the pressure is on the bowler at all times. I've seen him for all those years and I can't tell you if he has batted better."Kohli's innings also helped him break another major record. He went past Sachin Tendulkar to become the highest run-scorer in ODI run chases. Sachin had scored 8,720 runs in 242 innings while batting second in ODIs. His record included 17 centuries and 52 half-centuries at an average of 42.33.Kohli has now scored 8,741 runs in 169 innings in ODI chases. He has done so at an average of 66.21 and a strike rate of 95.03. His tally includes 30 centuries and 46 half-centuries.His record is even better when India win while chasing. Kohli has scored 6,477 runs in 108 innings in successful ODI chases. His average is 89.95 and his strike rate is over 98. He has scored 25 centuries and 30 half-centuries, with 183 being his highest score.There was another record for Kohli in the first ODI. He equalled former Australia captain Ricky Ponting's record for the most runs against New Zealand in ODI cricket.Both Kohli and Ponting have scored 1,971 runs against New Zealand.Kohli has reached this total in 37 innings at an average of 57.97 and a strike rate of 97.86. He has seven centuries and 11 half-centuries against the Black Caps.Ponting scored the same number of runs in 50 innings across 51 matches. His average was 45.83, with six centuries and 12 half-centuries.Kohli's latest performance added two more major records to his name and helped India start the ODI series with a win.

KOLKATA: A man allegedly beheaded his wife and sat inside a Kali temple with her severed head resting on his lap, while their two sons sat beside him, in West Bengal's South Dinajpur district on Wednesday.The accused, Rintu Ghosh, a former bus conductor, was found inside the temple in Ward 4 of Narayanpur, under Gangarampur, with a knife in his hand and his wife's severed head on his lap.The incident came to light after local residents spotted Ghosh inside the temple and alerted the police. The victim, identified as 35-year-old Seema Sarkar, had allegedly been killed before the accused brought her severed head to the temple.A police team led by Gangarampur police station inspector-in-charge Purnendu Kundu reached the spot and arrested Ghosh. Police recovered the woman's body and sent it for post-mortem examination.While being taken away in a police van, Ghosh spoke to reporters about losing his job with the North Bengal State Transport Corporation (NBSTC). He said, "After losing my job from NBSTC and going to the police station, I have become a psycho."According to a relative, Rajesh Pramanik, Ghosh had been struggling to make ends meet after losing his job as a bus conductor. He later tried his hand at small business activities but failed to find a stable source of income.Pramanik also claimed that Ghosh's lifestyle had changed in recent times. He had reportedly given up non-vegetarian food and turned vegetarian, while also displaying behaviour that the relative described as tantric.Police are interrogating Ghosh to determine what led to the alleged murder. Investigators are examining his personal circumstances, employment-related difficulties and recent behavioural changes as they try to establish the motive behind the killing.

Article Title: "Always worry about": Steffi Graf and Andre Agassi's parenting decision kept their two children away from the pressure of tennis stardom
Article Text:
Meet Steffi Graf and Andre Agassi's children, Jaden and Jaz

Open

Why Jaden and Jaz Agassi never pursued professional tennis

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Growing up with two of the greatest tennis players in history could easily make professional sports feel like a family tradition. But Steffi Graf and Andre Agassi had a different vision for their children. Despite building legendary careers and collecting some of tennis' biggest honours, the couple never expected their son, Jaden, and daughter, Jaz, to follow in their footsteps. Instead, they allowed both children to discover their own interests, build separate identities and enjoy childhood without the pressure of living up to their famous surname.Steffi Graf and Andre Agassi married in October 2001, shortly before welcoming their first child. Their son, Jaden Gil Agassi, was born on October 26, 2001. Two years later, on October 3, 2003, they welcomed their daughter, Jaz Elle Agassi.Although their parents spent decades competing at the highest level, the children grew up largely away from public attention.Agassi's own childhood played an important role in shaping his parenting approach. In his autobiography,, he described the intense pressure his father placed on him to become a successful tennis player.“My father yells everything twice, sometimes three times, sometimes 10,” he wrote. “Harder, he says, harder. Hit earlier. Damn it Andre, hit earlier, Crowd the ball, crowd the ball.”Having experienced that demanding environment himself, Agassi wanted something different for his children. Graf also made it clear that they were free to choose their own interests.“We never really introduced tennis so much into their lives. They’ve chosen other things,” the mom of two shared.Jaden Agassi found his passion in baseball rather than tennis. He joined the University of Southern California in 2019 and played college baseball before gaining experience with summer league teams. In 2025, he also represented Team Germany in the World Baseball Classic Qualifiers.His ambition is to build a sporting identity separate from his parents' achievements.“Agassi is a very tennis last name, of course,” Jaden told WKBN News in June 2024. “The goal is to try to make it a baseball one.”..Jaz Agassi, meanwhile, has explored dancing and horseback riding. She also enjoys outdoor activities, including snowboarding. Unlike her brother, she keeps much of her personal life away from public attention.Agassi has also spoken openly about protecting his children's freedom to choose their own paths.“The idea that a parent would attach a child’s right to be loved in this world based on their performance is a tragedy,” he explained in a 2024 conversation with USA Today. “What somebody needs to do to be pro at 16 years old is crazy, right?”..He once described tennis as an unusual sport and explained why he and Graf avoided pushing their children towards it.“It’s a weird sport,” Andre told Fox Sports. “We don’t see too many second-generation players. For us, it’s about raising our children in a way we can share in their life and not always worry about their life.”For the tennis legends, their children's happiness matters far more than another championship trophy.
Article Summary: Steffi Graf and Andre Agassi have two children, Jaden and Jaz. The couple never expected their children to follow in their footsteps. They allowed both children to discover their own interests and build separate identities. Agassi has spoken openly about protecting his children's freedom.

Article Title: Donna Kelce put her own happiness on hold to give Jason and Travis Kelce a better life, but her story of a mother's sacrifice goes far beyond football
Article Text:
Donna Kelce put her own happiness on hold to give Jason and Travis Kelce a better life, but her story of a mother's sacrifice goes far beyond football

What made Donna Kelce stay in an unhappy marriage for Jason and Travis Kelce?

Glamour

Kelce

Glamour

How did Donna Kelce balance her banking career while raising two NFL stars?

Glamour

Why did Jason Kelce’s retirement speech reveal so much about his mother?

How did Donna Kelce’s sacrifices help shape the future of Jason and Travis Kelce?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Long before Jason Kelce and Travis Kelce became Super Bowl champions and household names, their mother, Donna Kelce, was quietly making sacrifices that shaped their lives. She spent years balancing a demanding banking career, raising two boys with big sporting dreams and putting her family’s needs ahead of her own happiness. While the world now celebrates what her sons have achieved, Donna’s story is about everything she carried before they ever reached the NFL.For Donna Kelce, motherhood was never just about taking her children to school, attending their football games or making sure they had everything they needed. It also meant making difficult personal decisions, even when those choices came at a cost to her own happiness.Donna and Ed Kelce were married for nearly 25 years. However, their relationship had reached a point where both knew things were no longer working. Rather than immediately ending their marriage, they decided to remain together while Jason and Travis were growing up. They wanted their sons to have as normal a childhood as possible, without having to deal with the difficulties that could come with their parents separating.Donna explained this decision during her October 2024 interview withfor its Mothers of the Year feature. She said, “My husband and I knew that our marriage was not working, but we stayed together for the kids.”She also made it clear that their relationship was friendly, which helped them continue raising their children together. It was not a situation where the boys were left without support from either parent. Donna and Ed worked as a team, making sure their sons could focus on school, sports and their future.Ed also spoke about their decision in the 2023 documentary. He explained that separating earlier would have made it difficult to manage their sons’ schedules and provide the support they needed.For Donna, those years meant putting her personal life on hold. She did not hide how that affected her. During the sameinterview, she admitted, “But in that one respect, I did stand still for several years until I could move on on my own.”It is perhaps one of the most emotional parts of her story. She knew she wanted something different for herself, but she and Ed chose to wait until their sons had finished college and moved out before going their separate ways. Their marriage eventually ended, but their relationship as parents continued.While raising Jason and Travis, Donna was also building a career of her own. She worked as a commercial banker across several states and steadily moved into senior positions. Her professional journey was not something she wanted to give up simply because she had children.In fact, she wanted her sons to grow up seeing that a woman could have a successful career, earn her own money and make important decisions for herself.Donna spoke about the effort she put into her work during herinterview, saying, “I was a commercial banker for a bank in several different states. I wanted to get ahead. I worked really, really hard.”She was also a major breadwinner in the family, meaning that much of the financial responsibility rested on her shoulders. Between her job and her responsibilities at home, there was little room to put herself first.Jason later spoke about his mother’s career during his emotional retirement speech on March 4, 2024. He revealed that Donna had spent more than 40 years in banking, starting as a teller and eventually reaching the position of vice president.He also shared something about her childhood that helps explain where her determination came from. When Donna wanted to attend college, her father was against the idea. He believed she should become a secretary or a wife instead. However, Donna went ahead with her education and graduated from Ohio University.Her journey did not end there. She later earned an MBA from Baldwin Wallace University and continued working her way up in the banking industry.Jason said, “And from my mother, I learned the all too important lesson of never letting anyone tell you what you can’t do.”Those words carried a lot of meaning because he was not simply thanking his mother for supporting his football career. He was recognising the example she had set through her own life. Donna wanted Jason and Travis to understand that hard work and determination could take them further than anyone else’s expectations.For years, Jason and Travis watched their mother manage work and family responsibilities, but children do not always understand how much their parents are doing behind the scenes. Jason admitted as much when he spoke about Donna during his retirement speech.As he looked back on his 13-year career with the Philadelphia Eagles, Jason made sure to recognise the people who had helped him reach that point. His mother received special attention, not only because she had supported his football journey but also because of the life she had built before he became a professional athlete.He spoke about how Donna had grown up in a time when many women were discouraged from pursuing higher education. Despite the advice she received from her father, she chose to attend college and build a career.Jason also recognised her financial contribution to the family, describing her as the person who was largely responsible for providing for them.For a mother who had spent so many years making sure her children had opportunities, hearing her son recognise those efforts on such an important day must have meant a great deal. His speech also showed that the lessons he had learned from Donna went beyond anything he could have picked up on a football field.He had seen her face challenges without allowing them to decide her future. He had watched her work hard, take responsibility and keep moving forward even when life was not easy.That is why his words about never allowing anyone to tell you what you cannot do were so important. They were not just a nice tribute to his mother. They were a reflection of the person Donna had been throughout his childhood.Donna’s story is also closely connected to the relationship Jason and Travis share. The brothers grew up playing sports together, competing against each other and supporting one another. Their parents made sure both boys had opportunities to follow their interests, even as their sporting ambitions grew.Jason eventually became one of the most respected centers in the NFL, spending 13 seasons with the Philadelphia Eagles before announcing his retirement in March 2024. Travis, meanwhile, built his career with the Kansas City Chiefs and became one of the league’s leading tight ends.Their success brought Donna into the public eye, especially when she became the centre of attention during Super Bowl LVII in February 2023. With Jason’s Eagles facing Travis’s Chiefs, she supported both sons by wearing a custom jersey featuring their names and team colors.But that famous moment was only a small part of a much longer journey.Donna had been there through their childhood games, college years, NFL dreams and difficult moments along the way. Jason even remembered in his retirement speech how he and Travis used to watch each other’s games, sitting with their mother and cheering for one another.He described their bond as something that had made him stronger throughout his life. Their childhood was filled with competition, laughter, arguments and shared dreams of becoming professional athletes.Donna and Ed helped give the brothers the support they needed to build those dreams. Even after their marriage ended, they continued to remain friends and support their sons.Donna’s life also shows that supporting children does not mean giving up every part of yourself. She continued to build her career, stood by her decisions and eventually made room for a new chapter in her own life.Today, people may recognise her as the mother of two NFL stars, but Jason’s retirement speech offered a much deeper picture of the woman behind that title. She was a working mother, a determined professional and someone who wanted her children to grow up knowing that their dreams were worth pursuing.
Article Summary: Donna and Ed Kelce were married for nearly 25 years. They decided to remain together while raising their children together. Donna worked as a commercial banker across several states. She wanted her sons to grow up seeing that a woman could have a successful career, earn her own money and make important decisions for herself.

Article Title: “I am lucky that whole life, I have been surrounded by people”: How one Cincinnati coach helped Jason Kelce find his NFL future with a suggestion the Eagles legend never expected
Article Text:
How one Cincinnati coach helped Jason Kelce find his NFL future with a suggestion the Eagles legend never expected(Getty Images)

Paul Longo saw potential in Jason Kelce before he became a center

Jason Kelce's retirement speech carried a special message for his coach

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Jason Kelce's NFL journey did not begin with the promise of becoming a star. When he joined the University of Cincinnati, he was a walk-on linebacker with no major expectations surrounding him. He had to earn his place, prove himself and find a way to keep moving forward.But one coach noticed something in him that Kelce had never considered. Strength coach Paul Longo suggested that he try playing center. It sounded like an unlikely move at the time, but it eventually changed the direction of his career. Years later, during his emotional retirement speech, Kelce made sure to remember the coach who helped him find his place in football.During his March 4, 2024, retirement speech at the Eagles' NovaCare Complex, Kelce looked back at his early days at Cincinnati.“From Cleveland Heights, I entered the University of Cincinnati as a walk-on. As a linebacker, I had no idea what to expect,” he recalled.He also explained how little support or recognition he had when he arrived.“I had no stars, no investment from the team or the coaches. I'd have to earn everything.”Then came a suggestion that changed his career. Kelce remembered Longo approaching him during winter workouts.“Two weeks into winter workouts, Paul whispered to me in the middle of warmups, ‘You'd make a great center,’” he said.Kelce did not immediately accept the idea. Playing on the offensive line was nowhere in his plans.“I shrugged it off. Offensive line? Never in a million years did I think I'd play that position,” he recalled.Longo, however, saw an opportunity. He moved Kelce to the offensive line that spring, giving him a chance to develop in a completely different role.Looking back, Kelce did not hide how much that decision meant to him.“Paul moved me to offensive line that spring, and it ended up being the single greatest move that ever happened to me as a football player,” he said.Longo also had a different approach to coaching. Kelce remembered his motto as, “Work smarter, not harder.” He focused on helping players become stronger, faster and more explosive instead of simply pushing them through exhausting workouts.The most emotional part of Kelce's speech came when he spoke about the people who had supported him throughout his life.“I am lucky. My whole life, I have been surrounded by people that have believed in me – my father, my mother, my brother, Paul Longo, Howard Mudd,” he said.It was a meaningful mention. Longo had entered his story when Kelce was still trying to establish himself as a college football player. He saw a future in him that the young linebacker could not picture for himself.Kelce's words also showed that he had not forgotten the people who helped him along the way. His career brought him plenty of recognition, but he still made room in his final speech to acknowledge those who had backed him before the NFL spotlight arrived.The position change eventually helped him build a remarkable career. The Philadelphia Eagles selected Kelce in the sixth round of the 2011 NFL Draft. He spent 13 seasons with the franchise, earned seven Pro Bowl selections and six first-team All-Pro honours, and helped Philadelphia win Super Bowl LII.He also became one of the most respected centers of his generation.Yet, when Kelce looked back at the journey during his retirement speech, he did not only talk about the awards or the Super Bowl victory. He remembered the people who believed in him when he was still finding his way.For Longo, that quiet suggestion during a college workout became part of a much bigger story. And for Kelce, the coach who saw a center in a linebacker remained someone worth thanking years after their time together at Cincinnati.
Article Summary: Jason Kelce was a walk-on linebacker at the University of Cincinnati. Strength coach Paul Longo suggested that he try playing center. The position change eventually helped him build a remarkable career with the Philadelphia Eagles. Kelce made sure to remember Longo during his retirement speech.

Article Title: ‘Selectors could be forced to think’: Irfan Pathan backs Anshul Kamboj for 2027 ODI World Cup
Article Text:
Anshul Kamboj (Agency Image)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Former India all-rounder Irfan Pathan believes Anshul Kamboj has the potential to become a contender for India's 2027 ODI World Cup squad, suggesting that consistent performances could make it difficult for the selectors to overlook the young fast bowler.Kamboj impressed with the ball in India's five-wicket victory over New Zealand in the rain-affected first ODI at Auckland on Wednesday. Making good use of the seaming conditions, the Chennai Super Kings (CSK) pacer returned figures of 2/22 from his 10 overs, sending down an impressive 46 dot balls.His disciplined effort played an important role in restricting New Zealand to 185. Arshdeep Singh led the attack with four wickets, while Gurnoor Brar picked up three as India bundled out the hosts.India subsequently chased down the revised target of 143 in 22.4 overs, with Virat Kohli leading the way through an authoritative 74 off 51 deliveries.Speaking in a video by Cricinfo, Pathan backed Kamboj to make further progress, pointing out that his difficult introduction to international cricket should be viewed in the context of the circumstances surrounding his debut.The former all-rounder felt Kamboj had not been given sufficient recovery time after travelling before being pushed into Test cricket.The fast bowler made his Test debut last year as an injury replacement but endured a difficult outing, managing just one wicket while conceding 89 runs in 18 overs at an economy rate of nearly five.Pathan stressed that adjusting to different conditions, recovering from travel and preparing for the demands of Test cricket can take time for a fast bowler."He will be one of the bowlers for sure. What happened during the Test match, we have to understand. It is not easy to play a Test match after travelling. For any bowler to get adjusted to the climate, recovery and then go from there, it takes time. Anshul that time, needed more time to play Test cricket," he said.Pathan also highlighted Kamboj's versatility, particularly his ability to contribute with both the new and old ball. He pointed to the pacer's death-bowling skills, including his ability to deliver wide yorkers from around the wicket, which he has demonstrated while representing CSK.According to Pathan, having multiple skills at his disposal makes Kamboj a valuable option for the future. He also backed the youngster to climb the ranks if he continues delivering performances like the one against New Zealand."What I like about him that he can bowl with the new ball and has some good death bowling skill as seen with CSK. He can come round the wicket and bowl the wide yorkers. He bowled with the old ball in this match (against NZ in 1st ODI). He has that package, with the old ball, new ball and can nibble the ball too. He will go up the ladder as far as future is concerned. You would not be surprised if he keeps going like this, selectors would be forced to think about him as one of the WC probables.He is definitely one of them," he added.Kamboj's performance in Auckland comes after a challenging start to his international career, with his domestic and IPL performances having raised expectations before his India debut.His first ODI appearance against the West Indies at New Chandigarh was particularly difficult. The pacer conceded 82 runs in nine overs, with West Indies captain Shai Hope doing much of the damage. Hope scored 42 runs off 31 deliveries against Kamboj, including six fours.However, the disciplined showing against New Zealand offered a reminder of his bowling capabilities. With the ability to operate across different phases of an innings, Kamboj has now given himself an opportunity to strengthen his case for a longer run in India's ODI setup, with the 2027 World Cup on the horizon. The tournament will be co-hosted by South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia.

Article Title: ‘Sarah stood by him as a pillar of support’: Bhatkal family celebrates Abdul El-Sayed’s US Senate win
Article Text:
Abdul El-Sayed achieved a significant milestone by winning the US Senate race in Michigan





MANGALURU: The Jukaku family, which has roots in Bhatkal in Uttara Kannada district, is in a celebratory mood following Abdul El-Sayed’s historic victory in the closely watched US Senate race in Michigan.El-Sayed, a doctor, defeated Republican Mike Rogers to become the first Muslim elected to US Senate.The victory sparked celebrations in his in-law’s family back in Bhatkal from where his wife Dr Sarah Jukaku traces her roots.Sarah is the granddaughter of Jukaku Shamshuddin, who served as deputy minister for finance in the erstwhile Mysore State govt under chief minister BD Jatti.According to Sarah’s cousin, the family has been receiving congratulatory messages from people of Bhatkal.“It was a close fight marked by considerable hate and divisiveness, but the negative propaganda did not work. People stood united, and that is a big lesson and offers a new hope for India,” he said.“Sarah stood firmly by her husband as a pillar of support, and the couple worked tirelessly over the past 18 months. It was not an easy journey. However, El-Sayed stood his ground with honesty and conviction. The small donations and support he received also played a crucial role,” the cousin added.Several family members settled in the US travelled to Michigan to be part of the celebrations.The family’s WhatsApp group remained active throughout the night tracking the developments closely.
Article Summary: Abdul El-Sayed, a doctor, defeated Republican Mike Rogers to become the first Muslim elected to US Senate. The victory sparked celebrations in his in-law’s family back in Bhatkal from where his wife Dr Sarah Jukaku traces her roots.

Article Title: Olympic gold, Asiad medals stolen from hockey legend MM Somaya's Bengaluru home
Article Text:
MM Somaya, a hockey legend, faced a devastating burglary at his home in Bengaluru on October 28.





BENGALURU: Last Wednesday, when hockey legend MM Somaya returned from his morning walk in Apangela, near his hometown Madikeri, his wife Shami greeted him with news of a burglary at their Bengaluru residence.His first thoughts were about his most prized possessions - medals won for the country, including his gold medal from 1980 Moscow Olympics. He rushed back to find his worst fears confirmed. His house in HAL 3rd Stage had been broken into between 2.30am and 4am on Oct 28, and valuables worth over Rs 3 lakh, including four international medals, were stolen."I'm obviously very hurt because the medals are an irreplaceable symbol of years of dedication, sacrifice and service to the country," an anguished Somaya told TOI.The two burglars, wearing helmets, also stole Rs 30,000 in cash and gold and silver articles. They entered after breaking open the main door and were captured on neighbours' CCTV cameras."Apart from the Olympic gold, two Asian Games medals - a silver from the 1982 Games in New Delhi and a bronze from the 1986 Games in Seoul - and a Champions Trophy bronze from 1982 were stolen," Somaya (67) added.Neighbours alerted the couple around 7.30am, and they immediately left for Bengaluru.Police registered an FIR the same day and said they were confident of solving the case, citing strong clues."We have collected much CCTV footage from the area and have some vital clues on the miscreants. They had watched the house for some hours and, after ensuring it was locked, broke in. However, we will crack the case," an investigating officer said.Somaya, a former India captain, moved to the city from Mumbai in 2025 after retiring from Bharat Petroleum.
Article Summary: MM Somaya's house in Bengaluru broken into between 2.30am and 4am on Oct 28. Valuables worth over Rs 3 lakh, including four international medals, were stolen. Two burglars, wearing helmets, also stole Rs 30,000 in cash and gold and silver articles.

Article Title: Scientist builds a mini universe of 24,000 atoms to show time can be measured without a clock
Article Text:
Representative Image

Entropy, not a clock, keeps time in this mini universe

A scientist at the University of Birmingham has built a mini universe out of about 24,000 atoms to show that time can be measured without a clock. Giovanni Barontini's experiment tracks the order of events purely through changes in entropy, the measure of disorder in a system.The result matters because physics still has no settled answer on what time is. General relativity and quantum mechanics describe it differently, and this lab-made universe offers a controlled way to study that mismatch.The atoms are rubidium, chilled to almost absolute zero, which is around minus 273 degrees Celsius. At that temperature they stop behaving like separate particles and act more like a single cloud.The cloud sits in a trap it cannot escape. A specially configured laser splits the trap into two halves. One is the bright side, which was observed. The other is the dark side, which stays unobserved.Only the bright side served as the timekeeper. Its entropy kept changing, and the internal timer moved forward only when atoms crossed the laser barrier between the two halves. By watching the cloud expand and contract, and by tracking the exchange of atoms, it became possible to work out the order in which events happened.There was a catch. When no atoms crossed over, the internal clock stopped. An external clock kept running anyway, so the two disagreed on when events took place. Inside this system, time did not match the time outside it.The experiment could help link relativity and quantum physicsBoth theories underpin modern physics, yet they do not always agree on how time works. In certain quantum systems, for instance, time can be reversed. Showing that time can be read from entropy changes in an atomic system is a step toward bringing the two together.Barontini's model is only a starting point. It leaves out factors such as black holes, and several settings can be changed, including the shape of the trap, the density of the atoms and the height of the laser barrier.The cloud's repeated swings between the dark and bright sides could also help scientists simulate conditions just after the Big Bang. It might even help model the lead-up to the Big Crunch, the theoretical point at which the universe collapses into itself.The full impact will take a while to show. For now, it answers a simple question: you do not need a clock to tell time, as long as something keeps changing.
Article Summary: Giovanni Barontini's experiment tracks the order of events purely through changes in entropy, the measure of disorder in a system. The experiment could help link relativity and quantum physics. It could also help scientists simulate conditions just after the Big Bang.

Article Title: Hours after US mid-term election results, Elon Musk sends 'let's go to Space' message to Google, Amazon, Meta and other companies building data centres; says: Right now …
Article Text:
Elon Musk sends 'let's go to Space' message hours after mid-term election results

Democrats wins Texas

US mid-term election rewrites history

Hours after mid-term election results, Elon Musk said that building data centres in space look increasingly “appealing right now”. The post comes following the Democrats’ strong performance in the US mid-term elections. Musk, who has been a prominent Republican supporter during the election cycle and reportedly spent over $150 million in Texas alone, shared two posts on X (formerly Twitter). “Data centers in space looking pretty appealing right now,” Musk wrote in the early hours of Wednesday, November 4, after election results pointed to a major victory for Democrats.“Guess my election-interfering space lasers didn’t work this time 🤷‍♂️,” Musk said in the second post, appearing to joke about his political influence and the election outcome.The comments came as Democrats made significant gains, including a surprise victory in Texas’ governor’s race by Democrat Gina Hinojosa, who has opposed data centre expansion. Notably, Elon Musk and his companies – Tesla, SpaceX, and xAI have a growing footprint of high-performance computing (HPC), chip manufacturing, and data center-related infrastructure projects across Texas.Musk’s posts did not directly address companies such as Google , Amazon and Meta, which are expanding their data centre infrastructure to support AI development.The billionaire's remark on data centres come as the AI industry faces growing political scrutiny over massive data centers, with concerns about electricity costs and environmental impacts becoming campaign issues.The 2026 midterm elections in the US had a series of historic firsts so far. Voters elected the country's first Black woman governor, first Native American woman governor, first Native American woman senator and first openly gay male senator in the mid-term elections.The elections also set a records for women's political participation. According to Rutgers University's Center for American Women and Politics, nearly 300 women ran for the US House and Senate.
Article Summary: Elon Musk says data centres in space look 'appealing right now' Comments come as Democrats make significant gains in US mid-term elections. Tesla, SpaceX, and xAI have a growing footprint of high-performance computing (HPC) and data center-related infrastructure projects across Texas.

Article Title: The Diwali party code: Rishtedaar out, besties in
Article Text:
The polaroids adorning our friendly neighbourhood Bhaisaaaaab Vishnu Kaushal and gang's mirror proves that our parties look a lot more Insta-worthy

Inside Vishnu's Diwali hang

The behind-the-scenes of Gen Z party looks are decided very casually (pic credit: nirvana.escapes)

Mood boards

over dress codes

Themed parties make for great pictures

Potlucks

over catered meals





In our trendsetting stride, this festive season, we’re getting rid of Diwali parties filled with door ke rishtedaar and an awkward vibe that even the DJ can’t fix. Our parties are Instagrammable, aesthetic, and totally chill. With close friends, a few mutuals, and lots of snacks, there’s no pressure on the host to whip up an elaborate feast or to deck up the house. After all, Diwali is about sharing joy, not people-pleasing!Content creator Vishnu Kaushal hosts a Diwali party every year. After hosting a low-key event this year, he tells us, "Over the years, we’ve done everything for our Diwali party. This year was a lot more low-key, just with a few of our closest friends & family. Just with people we almost see every day or want to see every day!" Talking about how we do Diwali differently, he says, "For us personally, it’s about creating a sense of community with people we’ve met along the way. Diwali gives us a reason to meet; every other day there’s a friend’s Diwali party, and it’s the same people we saw at the last one. It’s a nice way to end the year together."The behind-the-scenes of our looks are decided very casually.“My friends and I usually coordinate outfits and build a theme around it. It's usually just a bunch of girls going, ‘Tere paas sari hai? Mere paas bhi sari hai. Cool, the theme is to wear a sari.’ Just like that, the theme is set: saris. Other times, it’s as simple as anchoring the night around a single colour,” Aastha Monga, 23 shares. For Prateek Aggarwal, 21, it’s about aesthetics, “I would like to have a traditional-casual theme that just matches the aesthetics and gets us some good content. It's more about the aesthetics and card parties for us.” Aamna Jain, 23 ,shares that her love for mood boards to plan the vibe, “Having a theme is a great idea because it ensures nobody feels out of place. Plus, themed parties make for great pictures! I love having a full-glam ethnic dress code for my Diwali parties. I usually plan the overall vibe for the outfits or create a mood board to give everyone some inspiration.”Aastha shares, “Honestly, parties are less about the food and more about the hang. If we have to eat, we just go out. Parties are for sharing embarrassing stories, making memories and dancing our hearts out.” Aamna adds, “A typical party would include warm decor, an absolute NO to fireworks, desi outfits, unique cocktails, some digicam pictures with the perfect playlist on hand. I prefer the snacks and a potluck situation. It acts as a conversation starter, and also reduces the load from the host’s back.”- Inputs by Annanya Bhargava and Mannat Saini
Article Summary: This festive season, we’re getting rid of Diwali parties filled with door ke rishtedaar. Our parties are Instagrammable, aesthetic, and totally chill. With close friends, a few mutuals, and lots of snacks, there’s no pressure on the host to whip up an elaborate feast or to deck up the house.

Article Title: Woman cop’s persistence brings 119 missing children home in 11 mths
Article Text:
New Delhi:





For families of missing children, the wait for a loved one to return can stretch into months, with every passing day bringing fresh anxiety and unanswered questions.At Jaitpur police station, head constable Chanchal has made finding those children her mission. In 12 months, she has traced 119 missing children, helping families reunite with the kids and bringing an end to the agonising wait.Posted at Jaitpur police station in South-East district, Chanchal traced 119 children and 16 other missing persons between Nov 2025 and Oct 2026. Of the children traced, 41 were below the age of 14, while 78 were between 14 and 18. The other 16 missing persons were adults.Behind each recovery was a trail of leads to follow, details to verify and agencies to coordinate with. Her work involved developing intelligence, using technical assistance, planning investigations and following up persistently on cases. She also coordinated with child care homes, NGOs and Child Welfare Committees across Delhi-NCR and other states to identify and trace the children.Police said her investigating skills and coordination with multiple agencies played a crucial role in identifying and safely tracing vulnerable children.For the families, however, the significance of each case went far beyond a police record. It meant a child returning home, parents no longer having to wonder where their son or daughter was, and families beginning to put their lives back together after a period of uncertainty.Her efforts also contributed to protecting vulnerable minors from exploitation and trafficking, police said.The South-East district police described Chanchal’s achievement as an example of humanitarian policing and a matter of pride for the district. Her work underlines how persistence, coordination and attention to each case can make a difference to families waiting desperately for answers.
Article Summary: Head constable Chanchal traced 119 children and 16 other missing persons. Of the children traced, 41 were below the age of 14, while 78 were between 14 and 18. Her work involved developing intelligence, using technical assistance, planning investigations and following up persistently on cases.

Article Title: Robin Minz’s maiden first-class century puts Jharkhand firmly in control against hosts Odisha on Day 3 in Bhubaneswar
Article Text:
Robin Minz en route his unbeaten century in Bhubaneswar on Wednesday (Pic courtesy: OCA)

Brief Scores: Jharkhand

Odisha





Wicketkeeper-batter Robin Minz slammed his maiden first-class century as Jharkhand post 433 for eight declared before Odisha reached 23 without loss at stumps on Day 3 of their Ranji Trophy Elite Group C match at KIIT Stadium in Bhubaneswar on Wednesday.Jharkhand resumed the day strongly placed and built on their advantage through overnight batters Aditya Singh and Minz. Aditya, who resumed on 94, completed a well-crafted 104, registering his second century of the season and second first-class hundred after his 147 against Kerala in the opening round.The visitors had been placed at 78 for four earlier in the innings before Aditya and all-rounder Anukul Roy orchestrated a recovery. Roy narrowly missed out on a century, scoring 89 off 140 balls with seven fours and two sixes to put Jharkhand in a commanding position.Minz, unbeaten on 11 overnight, made the most of the platform. The wicketkeeper struck 100 not out off 140 deliveries, peppering the boundary with 11 fours and two sixes. It was the first first-class century of his career after five previous fifties, eclipsing his earlier best of 79.Jharkhand continued to pile on the runs through the lower order as pacer Shubh Sharma produced a brisk 58 from 61 balls, including five fours and three sixes, helping the visitors cross the 400-run mark before captain Virat Singh declared at 433 for eight.For Odisha, Rajesh Mohanty and Lalit Yadav claimed two wickets apiece, while Ninad Rathva, Badal Biswal and Swastik Samal picked up one wicket each.Asked to bat late in the day, Odisha safely negotiated five overs to close on 23 without loss. Opener Swastik Samal was unbeaten on 17, while Gourav Choudhary was batting on six as Jharkhand’s pace duo of Shubh Sharma and Saurabh Shekhar failed to make an early breakthrough.With a first-innings total in excess of 400 and Odisha still trailing by 410 runs, Jharkhand will head into the fourth day firmly in control and eyeing maximum points from the contest.433/8 decl in 142.1 overs (Robin Minz 100 n.o., Aditya Singh 104, Shubh Sharma 58; Rajesh Mohanty 2/43, Lalit Yadav 2/86) vs23/0 in 5 overs.
Article Summary: Wicketkeeper-batter Robin Minz hits maiden first-class century as Jharkhand post 433 for eight declared. Odisha reach 23 without loss at stumps on Day 3 of Ranji Trophy Elite Group C match at KIIT Stadium in Bhubaneswar.

Article Title: Kolhapur’s pothole nightmare set to continue as contractors refuse repairs
Article Text:
A pothole on the road between Panchganga ghat and Shivaji bridge

Kolhapur

:





Residents are unlikely to get any respite from commuting woes this Diwali. After enduring bumpy, pothole-ridden roads through Ganesh Chaturthi and Navaratra, commuters will still have to navigate damaged streets, as several contractors have refused to start repairs despite receiving official work orders.Kolhapur Municipal Corporation (KMC) has approved 64 road repair projects worth Rs 62 crore for the 2026-27 financial year. Work on the ground, however, remains largely stalled, with contractors citing a steep rise in asphalt (tar) prices and claiming the projects were no longer financially viable.The deadlock has left the city’s roads scarred and commuters frustrated, turning what should have been a festive season into a test of patience for motorists and pedestrians alike.Social activist Amar Patil slammed the civic administration for the delay. “Roads that were supposed to be repaired before Ganesh Chaturthi are still riddled with potholes. Daily commuting has become a struggle. KMC must crack down on contractors who are refusing to execute the work despite receiving orders. At this rate, smooth roads in Kolhapur seem like an impossible dream,” he said.Responding to the criticism, KMC commissioner Rajendra Bharud acknowledged the standoff and urged contractors to either seek a collective solution from govt or begin work immediately. “Road projects covering 64 roads and costing Rs 62 crore have been approved. Contractors are, however, unwilling to undertake the work due to the increase in asphalt prices. They should jointly approach govt for a resolution or start the work without further delay,” Bharud said.With the prevailing situation, the residents may once again find themselves celebrating the festival amid traffic snarls, dust and potholes, waiting for roads that have been promised but are nowhere in sight.

Article Title: Video: Man sleeps atop 100-ft canopy overnight at Thane station, commuters mistake him for dead
Article Text:
Amidst the morning rush at Thane railway station, chaos ensued when a man was spotted sleeping atop a towering 100-foot canopy





THANE: A man who climbed a 100-foot-high Satis canopy outside Thane railway station and slept on top of it since the previous night triggered panic among early morning commuters, who mistook him for a body and alerted the authorities. Rescue teams eventually allayed their fears and brought him down safely after an hour-long operation.Passengers heading towards the bus station were in for an unusual sight when they spotted what appeared to be a body lying motionless on the semi-transparent canopy. They immediately alerted the police and fire brigade. Rescue personnel, however, struggled to reach the top of the canopy, which has no direct access route. Meanwhile, a crowd gathered on the elevated deck as teams worked out a way to bring the man down.“Rescue personnel managed to climb up to the metal ring supporting the canopy but could not reach the spot where the man was lying. Fortunately, the commotion woke him up. We persuaded him to carefully slide down the arched support to the ring, from where our team brought him down safely. One wrong move could have resulted in a fatal fall onto the deck or the auto stand below from a height of nearly 100 feet,” said a policeman at the spot.Yasin Tadvi, in-charge of the Regional Disaster Management Cell (RDMC), said authorities were investigating how the man managed to climb the structure without any support.The man, who was reportedly neither under the influence of alcohol nor mentally unstable, was later handed over to Thane Nagar police for further investigation. Preliminary information revealed that he had migrated from Amravati and was staying with his wife and child at Thane railway station.“Why he climbed the canopy remains unclear,” an official said.Meanwhile, commuters urged the authorities to take preventive measures to ensure there was no repeat of such an incident, which they said could also prove fatal.
Article Summary: A man climbed a 100-foot-high Satis canopy outside Thane railway station and slept on top of it since the previous night. Early morning commuters mistook him for a body and alerted the authorities. Rescue teams eventually allayed their fears and brought him down safely after an hour-long operation.

Article Title: TOPS chief Johal faces conflict-of-interest questions over wife’s role at Youth Olympics
Article Text: Pune: Questions of conflict of interest have arisen over Meenu Dahiya Johal accompanying Priyanshi Patil, the lone sailing athlete in the 35-member Indian contingent at the ongoing Youth Olympics in Dakar, as “coach-cum-manager” despite concerns within the sailing community over her coaching credentials.Meenu Johal’s husband, Nachhattar Singh Johal, is the Chief Executive Officer of the Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS).The contingent, which includes athletes from 11 disciplines, was approved at no cost to the government by the Ministry of Sports through a letter addressed to the Indian Olympic Association.The Times of India has a copy of the letter.The controversy stems from the fact that Meenu Johal, a former sailor, does not possess the requisite expertise to coach Priyanshi, according to people associated with the Indian yachting community.“Ms Meenu Johal competed in the Laser class, which is vastly different from windsurfing,” a former sailing athlete said.Another stakeholder in the sport highlighted the importance of having the right coach accompany athletes, particularly a teenage girl competing at an international event. For the record, Priyanshi is coached by Prakash Alexander.“Has Meenu Johal ever rigged a boat? Sailing can be dangerous.We are talking about a young girl going out into the sea, the weather can be rough. You need a coach who has the experience and who knows the athlete on the boat,” the stakeholder said.Both the former athlete and the stakeholder spoke to The Times of India on condition of anonymity.A spokesperson for the ministry said Meenu Johal was “an accomplished sailor and administrator of repute”.“She was awarded the ‘Engineer in Chief Trophy’ by the President of the Yachting Association of India in 2004 for being the Best Lady Sailor of the Year. She is also qualified, probably the only female, in powerboat handling by the Yachting Association of India, which is a minimum requirement for handling a coach boat on water. She had also qualified the written examination for International Race Official conducted by World Sailing,” the spokesperson told The Times of India in a written communication.The ministry’s response further cited Meenu Johal’s involvement in “talent identification, managing training, conduct of national championships and other administrative activities”.However, it did not provide details of athletes she had coached at the highest level of the sport.“Being qualified in powerboat handling is basically equivalent to having a licence to operate a boat,” the former sailing athlete said.“T293 is an entry level class of boats. It is not an Olympic event. But while T293 is getting approval for funding and assistance, events in the Asian Games and Olympics are not getting the same level of support, but that is what TOPS is supposed to be for,” the stakeholder said.It is also pertinent to note that the Johals’ son, Uday Veer, competes in the same Techno 293 event as Priyanshi, and that Meenu Johal has accompanied him as a parent during competitions in the past.“Optimist and Techno293 are junior pathway classes that provide progression to senior sailing classes. Hence, comparing the son’s participation in the Techno293 class with Priyanshi Patil’s participation in YOG 2026 is misplaced,” the ministry’s spokesperson replied to a specific query.“It is clarified that he (NS Johal) had duly disclosed the relevant details concerning his son and wife to the Competent Authority in the Ministry at the time of seeking approval for the tour,” it added.Yet, neither of the athletes concerned takes part in the optimist class.
Article Summary: Priyanshi Patil is the lone sailing athlete in the 35-member Indian contingent at the ongoing Youth Olympics in Dakar. Meenu Dahiya Johal is accompanying her as “coach-cum-manager” despite concerns within the sailing community over her coaching credentials. Her husband is the Chief Executive Officer of the Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS)
